causes.detail: reduced to other_known. Mapping: Known form: sequential greedy (local-MAP) Dirichlet-process / CRP mixture of conjugate Bayesian linear regressions. This is SUGS (Wang & Dunson 2011, 'Sequential Updating and Greedy Search'), the same scheme as the hard-assignment online CRP mixtures of linear experts in continual and meta-learning (Jerfel et al. 2019; MOCA, Harrison et al. 2020) and as online PWARX clustering. The neural phrasing is Mixture-of-Memories linear attention with R MesaNet memories and a likelihood router in place of a token router. Symbol by symbol: (1) Observation pair (regressor, target) := (u_t, v_t) = (Phi[x_{t-1}], Phi[x_t]). Phi is a learned feature map, and beta_t is a learned observation weight that drops pairs with beta < 1/2. (2) Cluster j's sufficient statistics := (P_j, K_j, N_j). P_j = (lambda I + sum beta u u^T)^{-1} is the posterior covariance of a Gaussian linear-regression cluster with prior precision lambda I and fixed noise variance s2. K_j is its posterior mean. N_j is its CRP table count. Updates u[3] and u[4] are the exact conjugate (RLS) posterior update of the chosen cluster only, as in SUGS. (3) Score S_{t,j} = ln N_j - ||v - K_j^T u||^2 / (2 s2 (1 + u^T P_j u)) := log CRP prior plus Gaussian posterior-predictive log density of v under cluster j. The predictive variance is s2 (1 + u^T P_j u). The constant and -(d/2) ln(1 + u^T P_j u) terms are dropped. (4) S_new = ln eta - ||v||^2 / (2 s2 (1 + ||u||^2/lambda)) := CRP new-table weight (concentration eta) times the prior predictive. (5) z_t = argmax_j S_{t,j} := the SUGS greedy MAP assignment. Mode birth := opening a new table, truncated at R components (truncated DP). (6) Readout y_t = K_{z_t}^T Phi[x_t] := the predictive mean of the most recently assigned cluster, applied to the current regressor. Logits Phi y := tied decoder. The equations coincide term by term except for the omitted log-det term in (3) and the cap R. Numeric check: reduction claim other_known (verified): numeric check confirms equivalence (max_abs_diff 1.341149413747189e-12) Critic's argument: Escape test, step 1: the broken invariant is real in the card's own equations. In u[1]-u[2], z_t is the argmax of scores that depend on K_j and P_j, so the slot that receives each write depends on the whole prefix. The bank is therefore not a sum of per-token writes. Two order-sensitive effects follow. MesaNet without decay is invariant to the order of the pairs, while this card's assignment of a young mode depends on order. With decay, MesaNet cannot keep rule A through 16 B writes. So the parent's linear-attention mapping does not repair. Step 2, repairs tried. The closest neural repair is Mixture-of-Memories linear attention (several MesaNet states with a hard router). Its router is a function of the token only, so it fails for the reason the card's Repair 1 gives: the identical key Phi[0] is routed to different slots within one sequence. Making the router a function of each memory's prediction error is no longer MoM. Content-addressed writes in a Neural Turing Machine are state-dependent, but they use cosine similarity to memory rows, not likelihood tests over d×d regression states. So no linear_attention, ssm, moe or hopfield mapping is exact. Step 3: why_unrepairable is correct against neural sequence families, but it misses the strongest reduction, which lies outside them. The update, routing, birth and readout are textbook sequential greedy CRP / Dirichlet-process mixture inference with conjugate Gaussian linear-regression components (SUGS). The score is literally log CRP weight plus posterior-predictive log likelihood, with the log-det term dropped. The card's own known_relatives concedes the PWARX, Mahalanobis-gating and sticky-HMM lineage. The same scheme with a learned feature extractor already exists in continual meta-learning (online CRP mixtures of linear-regression heads; MOCA). The argument holds against the parent but fails as a claim of novelty. It is a known online clustering/regression algorithm moved onto a token stream, so it is not radical.

causes.detail: reduced to other_known. Mapping: Repair the parent's mapping with exemplar-based leader clustering (Hartigan's leader algorithm, or BSAS with a point representative and an arbitrary proximity measure). Equivalently, use online sequential RANSAC with a one-point minimal solver. Neither needs a metric, a common feature space or a summed centroid. (1) The datum is the episode pair j = (x_j, y_j). The model family is learned: the hypothesis M_a instantiated from one exemplar a = (x_a, y_a) predicts, at any source x, the point mu_a(x) = E[x] + T(E[x_a] -> E[x]) delta_a. (2) The inlier residual of j under M_a is res(a, j) = ||mu_a(x_j) - E[y_j]|| = ||T_aj delta_a - delta_j||. That is exactly the gap in u1, so Pred(a, j) is the RANSAC inlier test res <= tau. It is also the leader-algorithm dissimilarity between the leader exemplar a and point j. Both families allow a non-symmetric, non-transitive dissimilarity, because only leader-to-point comparisons are made. (3) The anchor (x*, y*) is the leader / incumbent hypothesis, held as its minimal sample (an exemplar, as in Hartigan's leader and in RANSAC). m is its inlier count. u2 is leader assignment / inlier counting against the incumbent. (4) H is the outlier buffer (DenStream o-micro-clusters), holding singleton exemplars in a FIFO of size K. s_H counts each pending exemplar's inliers among buffered points: each buffered point is a candidate hypothesis scored on the buffer (u3). (5) u4 is hypothesis replacement by inlier support: a candidate whose support reaches the incumbent's count replaces it. This is the standard keep-the-best-consensus rule of sequential/preemptive RANSAC, evaluated online. Reinserting the loser into the buffer is ordinary bookkeeping that keeps a rejected hypothesis as a candidate, as in Misra-Gries / Space-Saving candidate replacement. (6) u5 is the one-pass inlier reabsorption / outlier-buffer re-check after a model change. (7) r1 is the K-slot FIFO exact-match cache (hard equality-kernel attention). (8) r2 is the decode of the incumbent model at the query, softmax(-beta ||E[v] - mu_*(x_q)||^2): a Gaussian-kernel output layer around the analogy completion. The completion itself is the parallel-transport analogy of computational anatomy (transporting a displacement from one base point to another, as in Schild's ladder / Lorenzi-Pennec). The connection is linear in the displacement and Rodrigues-exponentiated per SO(3) block. (9) The pretraining losses L_tr, L_sep and L_out are contrastive margin hinge losses on the inlier residual plus softmax cross-entropy: metric / model learning for the RANSAC model family. Nothing is learned in context. Numeric check: reduction claim other_known (verified): numeric check confirms equivalence (max_abs_diff 5.218048215738236e-15) Critic's argument: Checking the broken invariants against the equations: u1 is indeed a non-transitive pairwise residual with no common feature space, u4/u5 do keep an exemplar rather than (N, LS), and r2 is non-affine in E[x_q]. So the parent's centroid-based BSAS/BIRCH mapping no longer fits literally, and the card's rebuttal of the per-token gauge repair is correct. However, the card attacked the wrong repair. None of the three invariants is essential to the parent family. Hartigan's leader algorithm and BSAS with point representatives keep exemplar leaders and accept arbitrary, non-metric dissimilarities, because they only ever compare a leader with a point. Online one-point RANSAC is exactly the scheme here: an exemplar instantiates a hypothesis, Pred is the inlier test on the hypothesis' prediction residual, support counts decide which hypothesis is kept, and inliers are reabsorbed after a change. Non-transitivity of Pred is normal for RANSAC inlier relations and does not distinguish the mechanism. The card's RANSAC rebuttal lists only a learned hypothesis class, online operation, no refitting and order-dependent switching. These are bookkeeping and model-class choices, not a new update law. The query-dependent transport decode is the parallel-transport analogy from geometric statistics, now with a learned connection. The closest repair, and the one that maps, is online exemplar-leader / one-point RANSAC with a learned model class, an outlier buffer, a FIFO cache and a transport-analogy decode. The argument does not hold: this is a hand-assembled symbolic pipeline of known parts with a more expressive learned residual, and it would not surprise a researcher in those areas.
